newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC can claim some credit for strong price - Lukman.
newsitem.headline: OPEC can claim some credit for strong price - Lukman.

text.p: - OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said on Sunday he was satisfied with current bouyant oil prices and said the 11-strong cartel could claim some of the credit.

"Obviously if we let all the oil we can produce into the market it would be a different story. We're not letting all the existing capacity into the market," he told lobby reporters ahead of Wednesday's ministerial conference to discuss production levels for at least the first half of 1997.

In June OPEC set a production ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) but most members of the cartel, apart from Saudi Arabia, are producing at or near capacity, together pumping nearly an extra one million bpd.
Lukman acknowledged several OPEC members were busting their quotas but said the market was absorbing the extra supply.
OPEC's quota compliance committee, comprising the oil ministers of Libya, Iran and Nigeria and Lukman is due to meet at 1300 GMT on Monday, an OPEC official said on Sunday.
An early winter in parts of Europe and the United States was helping to keep prices strong, Lukman added.
"It's cold but I hope it gets colder," he said.

World benchmark Brent crude futures closed Friday in London at $23.05 a barrel, $2 off a post-Gulf War high set in mid-October amid Middle East tensions, low industry stocks and fears of heating oil shortages, but still about $5 above where they were this time last year.
Soaring prices have brought OPEC members an extra $30 billion in unexpected revenues and caused inflation jitters but Lukman said OPEC producers were not alarmed by the current market strength.
"The price is reasonable but we can't say it's too high," he said.
Asked if OPEC would discuss Venezuela's proposal to take account of domestic consumption when calculating quotas, Lukman said "It's something we can discuss but we have discussed it before."
